neet_che_u07_t01_1.working: BaO2 is a peroxide containing the O2^2- ion. Ba is +2, so 2x = -2 and x = -1.

neet_che_u07_t01_2.working: CrO5 has one oxide O at -2 and two peroxide linkages giving four O at -1 each. So x - 2 - 4 = 0 and x = +6.

neet_che_u07_t01_3.working: O in KO2 (superoxide) is -1/2. H in H2O is +1. O in OF2 is +2. H in CaH2 (metal hydride) is -1.

neet_che_u07_t01_4.working: KO2 O = -1/2 (II); OF2 O = +2 (I); O2F2 O = +1 (IV); H2O2 O = -1 (III). This gives A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

neet_che_u07_t01_5.working: A is false: H2SO5 has a peroxide linkage, so S is +6. B is true: in tetrathionate, two S are +5 and two bridging S are 0. C is true: O goes from -1 to both -2 and 0. D is true: Cl is +7, its maximum, so it can only be reduced. E is false: H is -1 in NaH. Correct set is B, C, D.
